T: They may take our lives. They'll never take our shortbread.
D: A Scottish commoner leads a rebellion against the English king.
P: Serve the mains when Wallace rallies the army before Stirling.
S: Highland haggis bon bons, whisky cream

Spiced lamb and oat haggis rolled into balls, crumbed and fried crunchy, with a whisky, wholegrain mustard and cream dipping sauce. Fry 400g lamb mince with a diced onion, then add 80g toasted oats, 1 tsp allspice, 1 tsp pepper, half a tsp nutmeg and 150ml beef stock and cook until thick. Cool and roll into 20 balls. Roll in flour, beaten egg and breadcrumbs and fry at 175C for 3 minutes until crisp. Simmer 150ml cream with 2 tbsp whisky and 1 tbsp wholegrain mustard for 3 minutes for the dip.
food for a march across the Highlands
Oatcakes of oats, butter, salt and hot water rolled thin, baked at 180C for 20 minutes, with sharp Scottish cheddar and apple chutney.
Scottish smoked salmon on brown bread with lemon butter, dill and capers, cut into neat squares.
M: a pot over the fire in the Highlands
Lamb neck simmered 2 hours with pearl barley, split peas, leek, carrot and swede, the meat pulled back in, parsley on top. Crusty bread.
Stirling venison with neeps and tatties

Venison backstrap seared rare and sliced, with buttery mashed swede, creamy mashed potato and a peppery whisky cream sauce. Boil 600g diced swede and 600g potatoes in separate pots until soft. Mash the swede with 30g butter and pepper, and the potatoes with 40g butter and 80ml milk. Season 800g venison backstrap with cracked pepper and sear in a hot pan 3 minutes a side for rare, then rest 8 minutes. Add 40ml whisky to the pan, then 150ml cream and 1 tsp cracked pepper and simmer 2 minutes. Slice and spoon over.
W: a tin of shortbread for the long march
Butter and sugar creamed, plain flour and a little rice flour worked in, pressed into a tin, pricked, baked at 150C for 40 minutes, cut while warm, caster sugar on top.
K: the battle cry, one word long

Scotch whisky stirred with heather honey, fresh lemon and hot water, with a clove-studded lemon wheel and a cinnamon stick. Raise it high. Stud 4 lemon wheels with 3 cloves each. Into each of four heatproof glasses put 40ml Scotch whisky, 1 tbsp honey and 15ml lemon juice. Top with 150ml just-boiled water and stir until the honey dissolves. Add a studded lemon wheel and a cinnamon stick to each.

s.note: food for a march across the Highlands
s.how: Mix 200g oats with 50g melted butter, salt and a splash of hot water. Roll thin, cut rounds and bake at 180C for 20 minutes. Serve with 200g sharp cheddar and apple chutney.
Mash 50g soft butter with lemon zest. Spread on 6 slices wholemeal bread and top with 200g smoked salmon, dill and capers. Cut into neat squares.

m.note: a pot over the fire in the Highlands
m.how: Simmer 1kg lamb neck in 2.5L water with 100g pearl barley and 100g split peas for an hour. Add 2 leeks, 2 carrots and a diced swede and simmer another hour. Pull the meat back in and finish with parsley. Serve with crusty bread.

w.note: a tin of shortbread for the long march
w.how: Beat 250g butter with 110g caster sugar, then work in 300g flour and 60g rice flour. Press into a tin, prick and bake at 150C for 40 minutes. Cut while warm and sprinkle with caster sugar.

d.note: the battle cry, one word long
d.how: Stud 4 lemon wheels with 3 cloves each. Into each of four heatproof glasses put 40ml Scotch whisky, 1 tbsp honey and 15ml lemon juice. Top with 150ml just-boiled water and stir until the honey dissolves. Add a studded lemon wheel and a cinnamon stick to each.
